title: Word order with onko with singular owners
summary: Build singular-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.
objectives: Build singular-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build singular-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.
Put onko first, minulla, sinulla, and hänellä immediately after it, and the basic singular noun last. This lesson practises that order.
keyPoints: Build singular-owner questions: onko + owner + one thing.

steps: Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put minulla next. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Put auto (“car”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.
Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put sinulla next. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Put pallo (“ball”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.
Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put hänellä next. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Put kynä (“pen”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.
Put Onko first to turn the possession pattern into a yes/no question.
Put minulla next. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Put peli (“game”) last: Onko + owner + thing. Onko already contains on; do not add another on.

commonMistakes: Keep Onko first and the owner immediately after it in the requested pattern: Onko sinulla pallo?
Reordering the words does not change fixed onko into a verb agreeing with the owner.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “Do I have a pen?” Put the owner immediately after the question word. Use minulla (“I as the owner”) and kynä (“a pen”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form.
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Possession question word order: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: onko + possessor + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.formation: On + the yes/no question ending -ko = onko. It stays the same with every possessor.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
kynä stays in its basic singular form: one pen.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Translate “Onko hänellä tyyny?” into English. You may use “he” or “she”.
acceptedAnswers: Does he or she have a pillow?
Does he or she have the pillow?
practiceExercises.explanation: Onko begins the question; hänellä identifies the owner and tyyny names one pillow.
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Possession question word order: form or meaning confused

parts.meaning: he or she as the owner
parts.formation: hän has the learned possessor form hänellä.
tyyny stays in its basic singular form.
